7.0.s.en: (1) David's desire to build a house for the Lord

7.0.0.en: Nathan the prophet: a prophet who lived in the time of both kings David and Solomon and recorded their lives (1 Chr 29:29 and 2 Chr 9:29). He was faithful in conveying God's word frankly without fear of the king's person, yet he also spoke with respect and esteem for David even while rebuking him.

7.0.1.en: A house of cedar: the cedar is the evergreen tree of Lebanon, and its fruit resembles the fruit of the pine. Its wood is good and has an aromatic smell, and it was used in building palaces and the masts of ships and in making statues.

7.0.2.en: Curtains: pieces of cloth from which the tent is made.

7.0.3.en: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied David his friend with cedar wood to build a house for himself (ch. 5:11), and David settled in it, as it was considered a royal palace. All things around him were quiet and settled, whether internally after the extinction of the family of Saul, which had been competing with him for the rule, or externally from the surrounding peoples such as the Philistines and others. It grieved David to dwell in a palace built of cedar wood while the ark of the Lord was in a tent of cloth, so he expressed to Nathan the prophet, his contemporary, his desire to build a house for the Lord no less splendid, if not more so, than his own house. This shows David's humility in resorting to telling Nathan the prophet about building a house for the Lord. He did not say to himself, "I am also a prophet, so why should I ask another prophet?" that is, he also forgot his position as a king.

7.1.0.en: Nathan did not consult the Lord about David's desire, but expressed to him his own opinion about it, approving this desire of his and assuring him that the Lord would work for the success of this endeavor, because the Lord had supported him in all his ways before.

7.2.0.en: Since Nathan hastened and agreed to David's desire to build the house of God of cedar, God spoke to him the same night to speak to David and ask him, "Shall you build me a house?" By this God commends David's desire, but shows him that He had dwelt in a tent among His people since the days of Moses, Joshua and the judges, and had not asked any of the judges, that is, after the people settled in the Promised Land, to build Him a house. The appropriate time for building a house had not come, neither in the days of the judges nor in the days of David.

7.2.1.en: We note that God spoke to Nathan and did not speak to David, for two reasons:

7.2.2.en: 1- Because Nathan was the one who hastened and agreed to David's desire, since it was logical and a beautiful spiritual desire, without consulting God, so God made known to him his mistake.

7.2.3.en: 2- To establish humility in David's heart, for although he was a king and a prophet, he needed to hear the voice of God through another prophet, in addition to His informing him through Nathan, as we shall see, that it would not be he who would build Him a house, but his son.

7.2.4.en: God also postponed the building of a house for Himself to declare that He had not given them victories over the enemies so that they would build Him a house, for He has no need of a house of stones and wood, but rather wants to reign over the hearts of His children. Although it was Solomon who built the house of the Lord, his father David was greater in God's sight and his heart was like the heart of God.

7.3.0.en: The sheepcote: the pasture of the sheep.

7.3.1.en: "From following the sheep": from tending the sheep.

7.3.2.en: The Lord did not want to frustrate David or make him doubt that He was displeased with him, therefore He did not permit him to build the house, so the Lord enumerated to him His kindnesses to him, which show His love for him. Indeed He began His following speech about him by calling him "my servant David," a title by which the Lord calls His chosen prophets who are faithful to Him. Then He followed that by reminding him of those kindnesses, which consisted in making him king over his people after he had been merely a shepherd of sheep, in addition to supporting him in all the works he did, giving him victory over all the hostile peoples and removing from him those who troubled him and his rivals, and giving him a name and renown among his people and the surrounding peoples also, so that he became one of the great men of history.

7.4.0.en: The children of wickedness: the wicked peoples.

7.4.1.en: After the Lord had enumerated His kindnesses to David, He mentions here His works, the works of the Lord, for the sake of His people. After the people had been wandering in the earth with no homeland, He gave them a homeland to dwell in, the land of Canaan, and established them in their homeland, so they dwelt safe and secure, no longer enslaved and humiliated by another people as they had been in Egypt.

7.5.0.en: God shepherded His people anciently. Whenever the pagan peoples attacked them, with the Lord's permission because of their departing from His way, God would raise up "judges" to deliver them by their means from their enemies, and in the time of David God gave His people rest and gave them quiet and stability. This is at the level of the whole people; as for David himself, the Lord tells him that He will bless his family, so that it remains in the forefront even after his death, as will come in the following verses.

7.6.0.en: "Which shall proceed out of thy bowels": your son born of you.

7.6.1.en: The Lord foretold him that when the time came for his departure from the earth and he died as his fathers died, his son who came from his loins would take the kingdom after him, and the Lord would support him and establish him on the throne of the kingdom. He said "thy seed" and did not say "your son," because He does not mean only the building of the house by the hand of Solomon, but also Christ, who will build the house that lasts forever, which is the Church.

7.7.0.en: The Lord made clear to him that his son who would take the kingdom after him was the one charged with building the house of the Lord, for Solomon the son of David is the one who built the temple of the Lord. The Lord also promised that the kingdom of Judah would remain and all its kings would be from the house of David forever. This means, through the true and everlasting kingship of the Lord Jesus Christ for ever and ever, as is said in (Lk 1:32-33), "and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end."

7.8.0.en: "If he commit iniquity": if he turns aside.

7.8.1.en: The rod of men: the enmities of the children of men and their transgressions.

7.8.2.en: The stripes of the children of men: the woes of diseases and crises that afflict a person.

7.8.3.en: God continues His words about Solomon and makes clear that He will look upon him as a son, so He will shepherd him and support him with special care, and the king is bound to God as to a father in a strong relationship. But the full meaning applies to Christ, who is His Son in essence and not by adoption as in the case of Solomon. Then He continues His words about Solomon and makes clear that He will treat him as a compassionate father treats his son, so if he turns aside from the straight way He will use disciplinary means with him, whether by exposing him to the troubles of human beings or to crises and afflictions, and this discipline will be for his good so that he may know his mistake and correct his way. But, says the Lord, I will not reject him or cast him off as I rejected Saul and took the kingdom from him and from his descendants, and so cleared the way for you. This was fulfilled with Solomon when he set up idols to please his wives, but he returned and repented and renounced all the riches of the world in the Book of Ecclesiastes. And when the sons of Solomon, King Rehoboam or those after him, sinned, He left them two tribes, and the kingdom of Judah continued after the kingdom of Israel, which had split off from it, for many years.

7.8.4.en: If some afflictions meet us in our life, let us not meet that with grumbling, but let us examine ourselves lest we have turned aside from upright conduct and God has permitted us some warnings to be for us an awakening to correct our course.

7.9.0.en: After your departure from this worldly life you will see with your spirit your house and your kingdom secure in progress and advancement, and the kingship will continue in your house a long time, in which all the kings of Judah will be of your descendants. This promise was fulfilled partially concerning David and his descendants, but the full fulfillment takes place in the person of the Lord Christ, who came in the flesh from the descendants of David to reign over the spiritual Israel, which is the believing people of God from all the nations, as an everlasting king with an everlasting authority that does not pass away.

7.10.0.en: The faithful servants of the Lord convey His message with all faithfulness and truthfulness. So did Nathan, and he told David all the words of the Lord which he heard from Him in the vision.

7.10.1.en: This is the mission of the servants of the Lord, which they are careful to perform with all faithfulness and truthfulness, namely conveying to the believers the Lord's message to them complete, without addition or omission, so that they may straighten their way and correct the course of their life in a manner that pleases the Lord.

7.11.0.en: "Sat": that is, he rested a little to collect his thoughts and then knelt or bowed down, or the opposite: he began with prostration, and when he grew tired of the length of prayer he sat and completed his prayer. The sitting is not meant literally, but rather settling and being present before God.

7.11.1.en: David entered the tabernacle of meeting and appeared before the Lord prostrate and prayed the following prayer: You have done great things with me, my God, which I do not deserve. Who am I but a simple shepherd of sheep, the son of an ordinary man from the common people, so how did You raise me to this position to be king over Your people?! We note in David's words that he was not angry or grieved because God refused to let him build Him a house, but on the contrary he felt God's great favor to him in all his life and His favor to his descendants in that He would permit his son to build the house of the Lord.

7.11.2.en: Before we ask more of the Lord in our prayers, we must first thank Him for all the kindness and care with which He has flooded us in our life. Therefore our Church, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, places the prayer of thanksgiving at the beginning of every ritual service.

7.12.0.en: "The manner of man": a wish that every person desires.

7.12.1.en: You were not content, my God, with these graces which You have poured out upon me, but You reassured me about what will happen in the future and for a long time to my descendants, and this is a wish that every person desires, to be reassured about the future of his children and grandchildren after him.

7.13.0.en: "Thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant": You know what is in my heart.

7.13.1.en: I find myself unable to express my thanks and my acknowledgment of the favors with which You have flooded me, and the promises You promised me and my descendants. You know what is in my heart, for You are the searcher of hearts and the tester of thoughts, and You know my weaknesses and my mistakes.

7.14.0.en: You did these great kindnesses which You promised would be for me and my descendants after me in honor of Your word, which is Your promises to me, and You informed me of them and made me know them.

7.15.0.en: Truly You are a sole and unique God in Your greatness, and there is no God besides You, and we learned that from what we heard from Your prophets and from our fathers, who saw Your works and experienced Your love for Your people and Your care for them.

7.16.0.en: "Terrible things": the plagues with which Pharaoh and his people were struck.

7.16.1.en: There is no nation on earth like Your people, whom You chose from among all the peoples, and You walked with them to rescue them and save them, and You gave them a distinguished place among the peoples, and their fame spread among them as the people of the Lord Jehovah, the mighty God of Israel.

7.16.2.en: David draws the attention of the people of Israel to the great works the Lord did for them, His awesome and fearful works such as the plagues with which Pharaoh and his people were struck, and the fear of the peoples of Canaan of His people whom He rescued from Egypt and drove out nations before them.

7.17.0.en: You, Lord, chose Israel as a people special to You and established them forever apart from the rest of the peoples. This was in fact fulfilled despite Israel's fall and dispersion throughout the world by captivity, for Israel according to the flesh ended with the coming of Christ, so those who belong to Him, that is, the believers in Him, became the new people of Israel, whom the Lord will establish in the faith to the end.

7.18.0.en: And now, Lord God, let Your promises be established forever with me and with my house, according to the word which You spoke to Your servant Nathan, so fulfill to us Your promises, and even if I sin or the members of my house sin, forgive us.

7.19.0.en: David prays that the name of the Lord remain great and glorious in all generations, so that everyone may know that the God of Israel is the Lord of hosts; he also prays that He keep his house established before Him so that it does not become extinct.

7.20.0.en: David said, because of Your grace to me, Lord, and Your promise to build me a house and establish it forever, I pray this prayer to You and thank You from all my heart.

7.21.0.en: David declares his confidence in God's promises which He gave him by the mouth of Nathan, then asks Him to begin by giving blessing to him and to his house so that it remains blessed forever.

7.21.1.en: May we trust in God's promises so that they push us to every good work, and not be shaken if afflictions meet us, for God's promises must be fulfilled. We only persevere in prayer and striving and trust that He will complete His work in us.

7.21.2.en: David's victories and his administrative organization. (1) David's victory over the Philistines and the Moabites (vv. 1-2) 1 And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines. 2 And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David's servants, and brought gifts.

8.0.0.en: The reins (Metheg): the bridle used with the horse, and what is meant here is control over.

8.0.1.en: The mother city (Ammah): that is, the capital, which is "Gath," the most important of the Philistine cities and close to the children of Israel, which had a fortified hall in which the chiefs of the Philistines gathered to plan attacking the children of Israel. Among the wars that David fought against the neighboring peoples and won was his war against the Philistines. It was not the first of the wars with them, for he had fought them before and defeated them, but they continued attacking the children of Israel, so this time he crushed them and subdued them and took the city of "Gath," the greatest of their cities, and by this the power of the Philistines was greatly weakened.

8.1.0.en: "Measured them with a line": the line was the means of measuring anciently, whether of lands or, here, of men lined up in a single row.

8.1.1.en: "Casting them down to the ground": he made the Moabites lie on the ground beside one another or sit on the ground in a single row.

8.1.2.en: "With two lines measured he": that is, he took two thirds of the Moabites.

8.1.3.en: "With one full line": that is, a third of the Moabites.

8.1.4.en: There was friendship between David and the Moabites when he entrusted his father and mother to them when he was fleeing from the face of Saul (1 Sam 22), but it seems that wrongs, treachery and hard conduct occurred from the Moabites, so David was compelled to discipline them so that they would not be a source of continual trouble for the children of Israel. He seized the captives and measured them with two lines, that is, after he put them in a single row on the ground, he measured with a line, then the same length of line again, and the remainder was equal to one line, so by this he divided the Moabites and killed two thirds and kept a third alive.

8.1.5.en: It is implicitly understood that he killed the violent and stubborn fighters and kept alive the elders, women and children.

8.1.6.en: By this David broke the power of the Moabites, so they became servants subject to him, bringing gifts, that is tribute, whether of silver or gold or the produce of the field or sheep or anything of their products. David fulfilled the prophecy of Balaam, "a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab" (Num 24:17).

8.1.7.en: David took the capital of the Philistines and broke the mighty men of Moab, so the land submitted to him. So be strong in your striving against the lust that dominates you or the sin into which you repeatedly fall .. hold fast to God with many prayers and fasts and give up anything that feeds this sin, and God will give you victory and subject your body and spirit to Him, so that you live in peace.

8.1.8.en: (2) David's victory over the king of "Zobah" (vv. 3-8) 3 David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates. 4 And David took from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for an hundred chariots. 5 And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men. 6 Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went. 7 And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem. 8 And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.

8.2.0.en: Hadadezer the son of Rehob: he is the king of Zobah.

8.2.1.en: Zobah: one of the kingdoms of Aram, lying north of Damascus and extending from Hamath in the west to the river Euphrates in the east. It is a wide kingdom and includes several small kingdoms, all under the control of Hadadezer.

8.3.0.en: Some regions of the kingdom of Zobah declared rebellion against their king Hadadezer, so he went to fight them to restore his authority over them. There was continual hostility between Israel and the kingdom of Zobah, so David seized this opportunity and attacked them from behind at Hamath and defeated them (1 Chr 18:2).

8.4.0.en: "Houghed the chariot horses": he commanded that their hamstrings be cut so that they become unfit for war.

8.4.1.en: In that war David captured huge numbers of enemy soldiers, reaching 20 thousand footmen and 1,700 horsemen, besides the chariots, most of which he destroyed and only 100 chariots were left, which is a small number not fit for war but used for transporting goods. David also commanded that the hamstrings of the horses be cut so that they become unfit for war.

8.4.2.en: It is mentioned in (1 Chr 18:4) that he took "a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen." The "thousand" here in the Second Book of Samuel means a thousand chariots, and the seven hundred horsemen mean seven hundred commanders of cavalry units, and the unit is ten horsemen, so the number of horsemen is seven thousand as stated in the Book of Chronicles. The omission of "chariot" here is customary for brevity, so the conclusion is that David captured 20 thousand footmen and seven thousand horsemen and took a thousand chariots.

8.5.0.en: Syria of Damascus: one of the small Aramean states. The Arameans possessed this city at the time of the rise of the kingdom of Israel, and it lies in the land of Aram, which extends from Lebanon to the Euphrates and from the Taurus mountains to Damascus and beyond.

8.5.1.en: There was friendship between the king of Damascus and the king of Zobah, so the king of Damascus went to help Hadadezer against David, but David defeated him and killed 22 thousand of his soldiers.

8.6.0.en: David appointed over the cities of Syria of Damascus what are known today as "military governors," so as to be safe from their rebelling against him and so that they would collect the tribute for him, and the Arameans submitted to his authority.

8.6.1.en: The secret behind all David's victories and successes and his deliverance from the plots of his enemies was the power of God supporting him.

8.7.0.en: Shields of gold: the shield is a sturdy metal disc used by the warrior to protect himself from the arrows that the enemy shoots. The shields of the soldiers of Hadadezer were of gold, or of wood overlaid with gold.

8.7.1.en: Betah: an Aramean city also called "Tibhath" as in (1 Chr 18:8). It exists now under the same name and lies between Aleppo and the Euphrates.

8.7.2.en: Berothai: a city in northern Palestine, now the village of "Brinan," which lies 10 km south-west of Baalbek, and is called Chun as it appears in (1 Chr 18:8). David took the golden shields that the Arameans use in war, and he also took from the two Aramean cities of "Betah" and "Berothai" exceeding much brass, and brought these precious spoils to Jerusalem.

8.7.3.en: All these quantities of gold and brass David afterwards handed over to his son Solomon to use in building the temple.

8.7.4.en: God's power supporting you cannot be overcome by anyone, however much the wicked gather against you. So do not be troubled by any threats, but remember the name of your God and beseech Him, and He will deliver you and protect you from all evil.

8.7.5.en: (3) The king of Hamath congratulates David on his victories (vv. 9-12) 9 When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer, 10 Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass: 11 Which also king David did dedicate unto the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued; 12 Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

8.8.0.en: Toi king of Hamath: one of the Hittite kings, king over Hamath.

8.8.1.en: Hamath: a small kingdom neighboring Zobah.

8.8.2.en: Joram: he is called Hadoram in (1 Chr 18:10), and he is the son of Toi.

8.8.3.en: The news of Hadadezer's defeat before David reached Toi king of "Hamath," and for him it was happy news, since there was enmity between him and Hadadezer caused by previous wars between them. Toi sent his son Joram to David to congratulate him on his victory, to inquire about his well-being and to pray for blessing for him, and he carried with him precious gifts, which were vessels of gold, silver and brass. David's acceptance of the gift shows that he was a man of peace and did not want war without cause.

8.9.0.en: Syria (Aram): they dwelt in Mesopotamia and then dispersed westward to many places. When we read in (1 Chr 18:12) Edom instead of Aram, that is because there was a treaty between Aram and Edom, so when David defeated them, the writer of the Second Book of Samuel wrote Aram as the more important in this alliance, and the writer of the Book of Chronicles wrote Edom because it was the more important in his view.

8.9.1.en: Moab: they dwelt east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea (v. 2). The children of Ammon: they dwelt east of the Jordan north of Moab. The news of the victory over them is mentioned in (ch. 10). The Philistines: they dwelt south of the children of Israel and east and south of the Mediterranean Sea, and the victory over them is mentioned in (ch. 5:17-25, 8:1). Amalek: they dwelt south of the children of Israel and the Philistines and north of Sinai. The news of the victory over them is mentioned in (1 Sam 30). Hadadezer: the victory over him is mentioned in (vv. 3, 4). The gifts that Joram presented to David, he set apart, together with the spoils he took from the peoples he fought, for the Lord, and kept them so that Solomon his son might use them in making the requirements of the house of the Lord, the vessels and their accessories, as well as the requirements of constructing the building itself and adorning it. The inspired text mentions some of the peoples who were the source of David's spoils and those who gave him gifts, namely: Aram, Moab, the children of Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, Zobah.

8.9.2.en: Thus we see how David prepared for his son Solomon, and helped him, in building the temple of the Lord, by the following:

8.9.3.en: 1- He fought the peoples who troubled the people of God and defeated them, so peace prevailed, which helped Solomon to build the house of the Lord.

8.9.4.en: 2- Accepting gifts and establishing good relations with the surrounding peoples who respect the people of God, and this establishes peace for the kingdom of God.

8.9.5.en: 3- He prepared the building materials that Solomon would need to build the house.

8.9.6.en: Just as David took care to prepare for the building of the house of the Lord by collecting gold, silver and brass, may we care not only for building our churches but even more for reverence and respect when entering them and during the prayers, so that we feel the presence of God and enjoy His work in us.

8.9.7.en: (4) The administrative organization (vv. 13-18) 13 And David gat him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, being eighteen thousand men. 14 And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went. 15 And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people. 16 And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder; 17 And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe; 18 And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the executioners and the runners; and David's sons were priests.

8.10.0.en: The valley of salt: south of the Dead Sea, also called the Sea of the Arabah. It is one of the places to which rainwater gathers in winter carrying a large quantity of salt, and when the water evaporates in summer the salt remains in the form of sheets.

8.10.1.en: A monument: a pillar or wall set up to remind of important things.

8.10.2.en: David set up a memorial monument on the occasion of his victory over the Arameans and his killing of 18 thousand of them in the "valley of salt," to be a witness to the great work of God with His people and a declaration before the hostile peoples reminding them of the power of the God "Jehovah," the God of Israel, who stands behind the victories of His people and does not permit anyone to harm them or challenge them. It is mentioned in (1 Chr 18:12) that the victory was over Edom, and as we mentioned, there was an alliance between Aram and Edom, so each book mentions one of the allies. The Book of Chronicles also mentions that the victor was Abishai, and this does not contradict what is mentioned here, because Abishai was one of David's military commanders.

8.11.0.en: Just as David organized the administrative aspects in Aram and appointed "military governors," so he also did in Edom, so as to ensure the stability of the region under his authority, so the Edomites submitted to David and paid him tribute. The inspired text repeats once more the Lord's support of David in all that he turns to of works, whether military or organizational.

8.12.0.en: David was truly a ruler chosen by his people; all the tribes pledged allegiance to him and declared their loyalty to him. He was a just ruler who showed partiality to no one in governing, neither he nor the judges appointed by him, so the people lived under his leadership in stability and security.

8.13.0.en: David appointed officials to the main ruling positions in the state as follows:

8.13.1.en: Joab: supreme commander of the army, which is equivalent to a minister of war and commander-in-chief today, so he organizes his armed forces to be ready to face any external aggression.

8.13.2.en: Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud: recorder, who records the official decisions issued by the state and the laws and regulations that the king decrees, in addition to recording the important historical events in the life of the kingdom and the king, of wars and victories.

8.13.3.en: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar: two heads of the priests who shared the service of the Lord. The first, "Zadok," for the service of the tabernacle of meeting, which was still in "Gibeon," while "Ahimelech" was for the service of the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which David had moved to Jerusalem. This appointment showed David's concern for the spiritual service for the sake of his people.

8.13.4.en: Seraiah: to organize the state's accounts and supervise the collection of tribute and organize the censuses. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada: commander of the royal guard and head of the infantry battalions under the command of Joab, the commander of the army.

8.13.5.en: The executioners: they are the keepers of security and guards of the king, and they also carry out the sentences of flogging on the guilty. In the time of David they were of the Cherethites, that is, the original inhabitants of Judea, and they used foreign executioners such as the Cretans so that they would not show partiality in sedition or sentences to any person because of kinship.

8.13.6.en: The runners: they are the foot soldiers; Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was their head in the days of King David. David's sons: what is meant here is not their being anointed to the priesthood or performing its rites, because that was limited to the descendants of Aaron and the tribe of Levi, while David and his sons were of the tribe of Judah. So the intended meaning of priests here is that they were counselors to their father, constantly attending him, and he describes them figuratively here as priests because priests are mediators between the people and God, just as David's sons were helpers to him and mediators between the people and him, that is, they cared about the problems of the people and met with their father to solve them. So the word priest here means a servant and mediator and not the Aaronic priesthood.

8.13.7.en: May every father and mother and servant or official in any place organize his responsibilities and involve others with him in them, and follow them up with patience, encouragement and firmness, so that he enjoys peace and growth in his spiritual and social life. David and Mephibosheth
